summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for evaluation of left upper extremity and back erythema, initially concerning for cellulitis. She had been started on IV antibiotics in the emergency department but was found to be afebrile with normal white blood cell count and lactate. Physical exam revealed non-contiguous areas of redness on the arm and back, consistent with skin irritation from prolonged contact with urine, leading to a diagnosis of contact dermatitis. Urine culture grew E. coli, but due to absence of symptoms, no oral antibiotics were prescribed. Her HIV remained well-controlled with undetectable viral load, chronic diastolic heart failure was stable, and warfarin was restarted for subtherapeutic INR. She was discharged home with topical treatments, a visiting nurse, and instructions for ongoing skin and heart failure management.
problems: Contact dermatitis and other eczema, unspecified cause
Urinary tract infection, site not specified
Asymptomatic human immunodeficiency virus [HIV] infection status
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
